fixes.explanation: You caught it, baker! The song says, "God is in her citadels; He has shown Himself to be a fortress." The fortress isn't a wall or an army. It's God Himself. I've spent years in a junk drawer, and I never once saw a fortress with a price sticker on it.
That's it, baker. The song tells God, "With a wind from the east You wrecked the ships of Tarshish." Notice the song says it straight to Him. One wind, and those ships were wrecked.

Right on, baker. The song says, "As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts…" What they heard matches what they saw. It's like hearing my cookies are great and then actually taking a bite.
Waiting is a reasonable guess, but that's not what the verse says. It says, "As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts…" They have seen it. This verse is a done deal.

True, baker! The song says, "God will establish her forever." The word is forever, and the song doesn't put an end date on it. Right after that comes the word Selah, and I'll leave it right there in the song where it belongs.
It's true, friend, and the song says so plainly. "God will establish her forever." There's no time limit on it. Forever means forever, and I'm not going to argue with the song.

That's right, baker. The song says, "Your name, O God, like Your praise, reaches to the ends of the earth…" That's about as far as far gets. I can't even get my cookie smell into the next room without a fan.

You got it, baker. The song says, "Mount Zion is glad, the daughters of Judah rejoice, on account of Your judgments." So the gladness comes on account of His judgments. Gladness and judgments in the same breath, and the song doesn't blink.

Treasures would be a fun party, but the song doesn't mention any. It says they rejoice "…on account of Your judgments." No gold, no jewels, nothing shiny gets named in that verse. Not even a single sprinkle.

Yes, baker! The song says to tour it all "…that you may tell the next generation." The walk has a purpose, and the purpose is telling. That's like me walking through a recipe step by step so I have something to tell the next baker.
It's true, friend, and it's right there in the last line. The song says, "He will be our guide even till death." That's the song's own last word on it. I'd say that's a good guide to have.
